1.0 Version History

- Version 1.3 (03/02/2011)

  • Added the Clockwork Vault puzzle solution and fixed two shop prices that were swapped. Rewrote the final boss strategy after some very helpful mail.

- Version 1.2 (11/20/2010)

  • Bestiary now lists steal tables. Corrected a north/south mix-up in the Bramble Labyrinth.

- Version 1.0 (08/14/2010)

  • First complete release.

2.0 Introduction and conventions

This is a complete walkthrough for The Ember Crown, an invented role-playing game that exists only so this document can test a guide reader. Every town, monster and item below is made up. Any resemblance to a real game is a sign that role-playing games have used the same ideas for forty years.

The walkthrough follows the main story in order. Each section lists the monsters you meet, the treasure you can find, and the shops in the area, followed by a description of the route and strategies for anything dangerous. General questions are answered in the FAQ at the end.

Slang:

ST:

Single-target. It hits one thing.

MT:

Multi-target. It hits everything on one side.

!Special:

Monster attacks marked with an exclamation point are physical specials, usually stronger than a normal Attack and often carrying a status effect.

For more on the conventions used by old text guides, see

http://www.example.com/text-guides (an example address that goes nowhere).

3.1.1 Harrowgate

Opponents: Hollowlurker (#1), Wispgolem (#2), Hollowsnapper (#3)

Container contents: Swift Boots, Camp Kit, Smoke Bomb, Antivenom, 2700 Gil

Harrowgate is where the story picks up speed. You arrive with Isolde, Corvin and Maro, and almost immediately somebody asks you to do something unreasonable. Save before you open that door. Trust me on this one.

Preparation: Put Maro in the Back Row. Physical attacks from the back do half damage, but Maro will be casting anyway, and you'll take half damage in return.

Monster formations:

  • (Outside)
  • Hollowlurker, Hollowlurker (10/16)
  • Wispgolem, Hollowlurker (6/16)
  • (Inside)
  • Hollowsnapper, Hollowsnapper, Wispgolem (11/16)
  • Wispgolem, Hollowsnapper (5/16)

Hollowlurker enemies are the ones to watch. They have a habit of using !Lunge on whoever is lowest on HP, and around level 4 that can finish off a weakened mage. Wispgolem absorbs Holy, so check your MT spells before you fire them off. As for Hollowsnapper, it is a self-destructive little thing with a 33 % chance to hurt itself whenever you hit it without killing it.

Item Shop:

ItemPrice
Smelling Salts90
Eye Balm60
Phoenix Quill600
Tonic40
Camp Kit900
Ether Drop1200

Stock up on Tonics. Nothing else here is urgent, and you'll want the money for the weapon shop.

Weapon Shop:

ItemPrice
Storm Spear1850
Hunting Bow1150
Moonsilver Blade1400
Quartz Rod1250

Buy the Quartz Rod for Isolde if you can afford it. It's a large upgrade.

Innkeeper: Rooms are 20 Gil. Breakfast is extra, and it's mostly porridge.

Isolde: We'll take two.

Hidden Items: There's a Antivenom in the barrel behind the well, and a Lucky Coin in the clock of the mayor's house. Leave the chest in the cellar alone for now; its contents change into something much better later in the game, and you'll come back this way anyway.

When you're ready, head west out of Harrowgate. The Ember Crown itself is mentioned for the first time here, in a conversation that is easy to miss. It's worth reading all of it.

3.1.2 Traveling to the Old Quarry

Opponents: Wispbeak (#4), Rustmoth (#5), Gravegolem (#6)

Container contents: Ether Drop, Smoke Bomb, Owl Pendant, Stillwater Bead, 2600 Gil

Traveling to the Old Quarry is where the story picks up speed. You arrive with Maro, Pell and Tamsin, and almost immediately somebody asks you to do something unreasonable. Somebody on the message boards swears there's a secret here. There isn't.

Preparation: Put Tamsin in the Back Row. Physical attacks from the back do half damage, but Tamsin will be casting anyway, and you'll take half damage in return.

Monster formations:

  • (Outside)
  • Wispbeak, Wispbeak (10/16)
  • Rustmoth, Wispbeak (6/16)
  • (Inside)
  • Gravegolem, Gravegolem, Rustmoth (11/16)
  • Rustmoth, Gravegolem (5/16)

Wispbeak enemies are the ones to watch. They have a habit of using !Lunge on whoever is lowest on HP, and around level 5 that can finish off a weakened mage. Rustmoth absorbs Water, so check your MT spells before you fire them off. As for Gravegolem, it is a self-destructive little thing with a 33 % chance to hurt itself whenever you hit it without killing it.

At the crossroads you'll get two options:

  • Take the cliff path.
  • Take the river path.

The cliff path is shorter but has twice as many encounters. The river path has a hidden chest behind the waterfall with a Ward Charm, which is worth the detour.

Hidden Items: There's a Camp Kit in the barrel behind the well, and a Stillwater Bead in the clock of the mayor's house. Leave the chest in the cellar alone for now; its contents change into something much better later in the game, and you'll come back this way anyway.

When you're ready, head north out of Harrowgate. The Ember Crown itself is mentioned for the first time here, in a conversation that is easy to miss. It's worth reading all of it.

3.2.4 The battle with the Gloomlurker Queen

Gloomlurker Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read this section first.

Gloomlurker Queen

  • Level: 14, HP: 17010, MP: 168
  • Steal: Hi-Tonic (rare), Hi-Tonic (common), Win: Smelling Salts (always)
  • Weakness: Fire
  • Special: !Spit: sets Confuse, Attack x 1.5
  • Vulnerable to: Blind, Silence, Stop
  • Attacks: Attack, Chill Touch, Tidal Rush

Open with Isolde casting a Fire spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Wren on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will flatten anyone below about 300 HP. When Gloomlurker Queen says "You cannot burn what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack pattern, so stop using physical attacks for one turn.

Note: if you are beyond the shame of any adventurer, you can steal a rare item here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your dignity.

3.6.4 The battle with the Wispsnapper Queen

Wispsnapper Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read this section first.

Wispsnapper Queen

  • Level: 26, HP: 93600, MP: 208
  • Steal: Ether Drop (rare), Smoke Bomb (common), Win: Ether Drop (always)
  • Weakness: Holy
  • Special: !Spit: sets Slow, Attack x 1.5
  • Vulnerable to: Silence, Sleep, Doom, Confuse
  • Attacks: Attack, Gale Slash, Tidal Rush

Open with Maro casting a Holy spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Pell on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will flatten anyone below about 660 HP. When Wispsnapper Queen says "You cannot burn what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack pattern, so stop using physical attacks for one turn.

Note: if you are beyond the shame of any adventurer, you can steal a rare item here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your dignity.

3.7.4 The Clockwork Vault puzzle, explained slowly and with considerable patience for everyone involved

The vault has four dials, and each one rotates the two next to it. The game never explains this. Set them in this order:

DialTurnsFacing
North2Sun
East1Moon
South3Star
West0Sun

If you get it wrong, a Rustgolem drops from the ceiling. It is not hard, just embarrassing.

The Ashen Spire is where the story picks up speed. You arrive with Isolde, Pell and Tamsin, and almost immediately somebody asks you to do something unreasonable. Save before you open that door. Trust me on this one.

When you're ready, head south out of Lantern Rest. The Ember Crown itself is mentioned for the first time here, in a conversation that is easy to miss. It's worth reading all of it.

3.10.4 The battle with the Rustsnapper Queen

Rustsnapper Queen waits at the bottom of the stairs, and the game is not subtle about it: the floor is covered in the bones of adventurers who did not read this section first.

Rustsnapper Queen

  • Level: 38, HP: 148770, MP: 1520
  • Steal: Smoke Bomb (rare), Smoke Bomb (common), Win: Phoenix Quill (always)
  • Weakness: Wind
  • Special: !Crush: sets Sleep, Attack x 1.5
  • Vulnerable to: Silence, Slow, Doom, Poison
  • Attacks: Attack, Rockfall, Chill Touch

Open with Pell casting a Wind spell; it does nearly double damage. Keep Tamsin on healing duty, because the second phase starts with an MT attack that will flatten anyone below about 1020 HP. When Rustsnapper Queen says "You cannot burn what is already ash!", it is about to switch to its counter-attack pattern, so stop using physical attacks for one turn.

Note: if you are beyond the shame of any adventurer, you can steal a rare item here with enough patience. It costs about twenty minutes and most of your dignity.

6.0 Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Can I go back to Harrowgate after the bridge collapses? A: Yes, once you have the airship. The bridge itself is gone for good.

Q: Is the Crown Edge worth the trouble?

A: It's the strongest sword in the game, so yes, but only if you enjoy fighting the same monster forty times in a row for a rare drop.

Q: Why does my save file say 'Chapter 0'?

A: That's a known bug if you save during the opening cutscene. It's harmless.
